subject: Energy
title: Energy vs. Power
description: A 60-second lesson on Energy vs. Power.

hook.text: A marathon runner and a sprinter both use energy—but the sprinter uses it much faster. That difference is power.

buildup.text: Energy is the total amount of work done. Power is how fast that work happens—energy per unit of time.

discovery.text: A 100-watt bulb uses 100 joules every second. Leave it on for an hour and it consumes 360,000 joules.

twist.text: A lightning bolt delivers about 1 billion joules in a fraction of a second—enormous power, brief energy burst.

climax.text: Your electricity bill charges for kilowatt-hours—that's energy (power × time), not power alone.

punchline.text: Energy is how much; power is how fast.

quiz.question: What does your electricity bill actually measure?
